newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes lower in US amid mixed mark/cross trade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes lower in US amid mixed mark/cross trade.

text.p: After rising overseas the dollar closed weaker, with a mixed performance of the German mark in Europe sapping enthusiasm for the U.S. currency, dealers said.

Mark/French franc rose to a seven-week high at 3.3958, despite a joint effort by French and German officials to calm fears of a French franc devaluation sparked by recent remarks by former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing.
But the mark fell to a 31-month low at 2.5336 per pound while mark/lira fell to 995.03 its lowest level in a month, in early trade.
"There is a lot of uncertainty in Europe ... that is really preventing dollar/mark from taking its own direction," said Kisoo Park, a senior trader at Bank of Boston.
The dollar closed at 111.23/28 yen and at 1.4977/82 marks, down from 111.70/75 yen and 1.5015/25 at the start of trade.
Giscard d'Estaing was quoted on Wednesday in the weekly magazine l'Express calling for French franc depreciation before France joins the proposed European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
A weaker franc might revive French growth by making French exports more attractive.
Although Giscard d'Estaing now wields little real political power, his remarks carry weight because he was a founding father of the EMU concept, along with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
Weak growth and high unemployment have fueled broad domestic discontent in France, triggering strong opposition to the budget slashing seen necessary for French EMU entry.
The mark's rise against the French franc indirectly helped weaken dollar/mark in U.S. trade, dealers said.

However, in an effort at damage control on Thursday, Chancellor Kohl and French Prime Minister Alain Juppe issued a statement implicitly rejecting the former French president's questioning of France's "stubborn" determination to keep the franc tied to the mark.
"More recently, Giscard seems to have retracted his call for 3.65 on mark/Paris, after a 75-minute conversation with Helmut Kohl," said David Gilmore, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
Dollar/yen traded quietly, with solid bids adding support under 111.30 in the U.S. session.
Meanwhile, the mark weakened against the lira amid speculation that Italy might rejoin Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) in the coming days, pegged at a stronger exchange rate against the mark.

The lira's rise this week stemmed from an article in Tuesday's Le Monde newspaper, which said French and other governments sought a lira ERM entry at 950 and were irritated by Bank of Italy market intervention to cap the lira.
Investors have also favored Italy and the U.K. because of the high interest rates available there and traders said EMU convergence trades in Europe were still in vogue.
"Sterling overall is one of the high-yielding currencies," Park said. "All the high-yielders are still doing well."
The pound surged to yet another four-year high at $1.6905. After some profit taking it ended at $1.6890/00, up from $1.6832/42 at the open.
The dollar closed at 1.2660/70 Swiss francs, down from 1.2690/00 Swiss and at Canadian $1.3391/96, versus C$1.3389/94.
The Australian dollar surged to a six-year high at $0.8123 before closing at $0.8113/18, up from $0.8100/05.
